title: Quadratic class and unit groups
objective: Complete public quadratic routing with Minkowski triviality certificates, narrow class groups, rigorous regulators, imaginary ideal maps, and benchmarked Buchmann-Hecke crossover policies

handoff.summary: Completed the public degree-two routes on main 786fb703. Ordinary class_group/class_number now use an exact Minkowski-bound short circuit for D=12 and the imaginary D=-3/-4 cases, with a replayable certificate and no factor-base or reduced-form materialization. NumberField.narrow_class_group exposes exact real quadratic narrow groups and returns the ordinary group for imaginary fields. Real quadratic regulator(prec) now returns the shared rigorous Arb-backed RegulatorEnclosure at the requested arbitrary precision rather than the old binary64 wrapper. The canonical ideal-lattice inverse map now covers imaginary integral, inverse, and scalar-fractional ideals under standard and translated presentations. Inspectable routing plans keep certified imaginary FLINT forms through the measured |D|=1,000,000,007 pilot and real forms through the exact 5,000,000-candidate resource cap; larger ordinary auto requests select the shared Buchmann-Hecke relation engine, while forced form requests fail preflight. Focused public tests, strict 208-module checks, and the relevant native FLINT qqbar/Arb test pass on linux-x64.
risks: Large real narrow class groups remain explicitly limited to exhaustive reduced forms and the default 5,000,000 candidate checks. The shared Buchmann-Hecke engine presents ordinary classes only, so exceeding the narrow cap returns an inspectable unsupported plan and fails before work; no narrow relation backend is claimed.

Specialized real quadratic forms still materialize all reduced forms and do not implement compact real NUCOMP. This is not an ordinary large-discriminant completion blocker because auto routes beyond the cap to Buchmann-Hecke, but users explicitly forcing quadratic-forms are capability-bounded.

The rigorous public regulator depends on the existing native FLINT qqbar/Arb adapter. Its focused native test passes here, but platforms without that optional adapter do not have an arbitrary-precision dynamic fallback in this lane.

Fundamental-discriminant validation beyond unsigned 64-bit range remains exact trial division and can be slow; the class-group auto route itself avoids exhaustive forms, but enormous real unit computations still need a mature arbitrary-precision factoring backend for uniformly fast validation.

QuadraticClassRoutingPlan.proof_status certifies the deterministic routing/cap decision, not the eventual proof label of a Buchmann-Hecke result. The general engine retains ownership of unconditional versus GRH-conditional proof semantics.
Only linux-x64 was executed in this lane; native Windows x64, Linux arm64, and macOS arm64 validation remains a central integration responsibility.
next_steps: Run pnpm test:changed, the complete pnpm test:native matrix, and exact-revision four-platform CI after integration. Local builds repeatedly passed stages 1-6; stage 7 native-kernel publication was stopped after it did not finish promptly, while the focused packages/flint exact-algebra test passed.
If large narrow quadratic groups become a product requirement, extend the general relation engine with oriented/narrow presentations rather than raising the exhaustive cap.
If environments without native FLINT must support high-precision regulators, add a rigorously rounded dynamic transcendental fallback and differential-test it against Arb.
